reason: E1 supports the role of semi-coherent boundaries in reducing pile-ups and balancing strength-ductility, but does not address recrystallization. E2 directly demonstrates that phase-selective recrystallization of the soft phase in a eutectic HEA eliminates weak boundaries, fully releases strain hardening, and achieves ~35% uniform elongation at ~2 GPa true stress, which aligns with the hypothesis's key premises. The cited evidence accurately represents the proposed mechanism and outcomes, with no contradictions.
premises: Dislocation pile-ups at semi-coherent phase boundaries in eutectic HEAs cause stress concentrations and microcracking, limiting ductility.
Phase-selective recrystallization of the soft phase in a duplex alloy can eliminate weak boundaries and fully release strain hardening capacity.
Recrystallizing the ductile FCC phase refines its grain structure and reduces dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
The hard phase skeleton remains intact during selective recrystallization, preserving strong phase boundaries and strength.
The resulting microstructure achieves high ductility (~35% uniform elongation) while maintaining high strength (~2 GPa true stress).
